sections.en: Opening: The Authority of the Jewish Calendar

p: בְּסִיַּעְתָּא דִשְׁמַיָּא, שְׁנַת הַתַּרְ"בּ, פֹּה קְהִלַּת וְלָאדָאװקֶע.
With the help of Heaven, the year 5602 (1842), here in the community of Włodawka.
כָּתַב בַּעַל הַקּוּנְטְרֵס "מְגִילַּת טַעֲנוֹת",
The author of the pamphlet 'Megillat Ta'anot' wrote,
וּבוֹ יְבוֹאַר וְכוּלֵי,
and therein it is set forth, etc.,
וְשֶׁאֵין אָנוּ יוֹצְאִים כְּלָל יְדֵי חוֹבַת הַמּוֹעֲדִים וְכוּלֵי.
and that we do not fulfill at all our obligations of the appointed festivals, etc.
אָמַר הַכּוֹתֵב, זְעֵירָא וְיַנְקָא דְּחַבְרַיָּא,
Spoke the writer, the youngest and humblest of the companions,
צָדוֹק בֶּהָגָאוֹן אֲדוֹנִי אָבִי מוֹרִי וְרַבִּי הַמְּנוֹחַ מוֹרֵנוּ הָרַב רַבִּי יִצְחָק כֹּהֵן זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא:
Tzadok, son of the Gaon, my master, father, teacher, and rabbi, the late our teacher Rabbi Yitzchak Cohen, of blessed and holy memory for the life of the World to Come:
קַנֹּא קִנֵּאתִי לִיסוֹדֵי הַדָּת וְהָאֱמוּנָה,
I have been exceedingly zealous for the foundations of religion and faith,
וּלְעִיקָּרֵי הַתּוֹרָה וַאֲשֶׁר הֵמָּה לָהּ לְאֶבֶן פִּנָּה;
and for the fundamental principles of the Torah which serve as its chief cornerstone;
וְהוּא קִדּוּשׁ הַחֳדָשִׁים וּקְבִיעוּת הַמּוֹעֲדִים,
namely the sanctification of the new moons and the determination of the festivals,

Explanation — Kiddush HaChodesh and keviat ha-moadim Kiddush HaChodesh means formally sanctifying the beginning of a Hebrew month; keviat ha-moadim means establishing when the festivals occur. Since biblical festival dates are tied to particular days of Hebrew months, deciding the start of each month has direct consequences for the dates of the festivals. The central dispute in this work concerns how that determination was made historically and how it is made in the fixed calendar.
Sefaria connections (editorial): Exodus 12:2 · Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 2:7
אֲשֶׁר הַרְבֵּה חוּקֵי הַתּוֹרָה וּמִשְׁפָּטִים תְּלוּיִם בָּהֶם;
upon which depend numerous statutes and ordinances of the Torah;
וַאֲשֶׁר בָּהֶם נִתְפָּאַרְנוּ נֶגֶד כָּל הָעַמִּים,
and regarding which we have gloried before all nations,
כִּי בְּכָל הַזְּמַן הָרַב לֹא נִמְצָא כּוֹשֵׁל
for across all this vast expanse of time no fault was found
בַּחֶשְׁבּוֹן הַנִּקְבָּע וּמוּסָד לָנוּ מִפִּי קַדְמוֹנֵינוּ הַחֲכָמִים זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה;
within the astronomical calendar calculation established and founded for us by our ancient Sages of blessed memory;
וַאֲשֶׁר בָּהֶם אָנוּ מִתְחַזְּקִים נֶגֶד הֲמוֹנֵי הַצַּדּוֹקִים הַמַּכְחִישִׁים תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
and through which we fortify ourselves against the multitudes of Sadducees and Karaites who deny the Oral Torah.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁזָּכַר בָּאַבְרַבַּנְאֵל (פָּרָשַׁת בֹּא יב, ב) עַל פָּסוּק: "הַחֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה לָכֶם",
And as Don Isaac Abarbanel noted (Parashat Bo, Exodus 12:2) on the verse: “This month shall be unto you”:
כִּי הוֹכָחָה עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה מִקְּבִיעוּת הַחֳדָשִׁים וְהַמּוֹעֲדִים,
that an undeniable proof for the Oral Torah derives from the establishment of months and festivals,
שֶׁלֹּא נִזְכַּר כְּלָל בַּכָּתוּב,
which is not delineated at all in the written Scripture,
וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ סָמַךְ עַצְמוֹ עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
and perforce Scripture relied upon the Oral Torah.
וְהָרַב בַּעַל "צִלְיוֹן לְעֵינַיִם חֲכָמִים" (הַצְּלָ"ח) בְּהַקְדָּמָתוֹ הוֹסִיף לוֹמַר,
And the author of the Tzelach (Rabbi Yechezkel Landau) in his introduction added:
שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ אִם נִתְעַקֵּשׁ וְנֹאמַר שֶׁמִּמֵּילָא נֵדַע,
that even should we stubbornly argue that we would know naturally,
בִּהְיוֹת הַחֹדֶשׁ לַלְּבָנָה כָּל אֵימַת שֶׁמִּתְחַדֶּשֶׁת,
since the month follows the moon whenever it renews itself,
וְהַשָּׁנָה לַחַמָּה, וּשְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה פַּעַם מִתְחַדֶּשֶׁת הַלְּבָנָה בָּהּ,
and the year follows the solar cycle wherein the moon renews twelve times,
עֲדַיִן מַה נַּעֲשֶׂה לְאַחַד עָשָׂר יוֹם הַיְּתֵירִים,
yet what should we do with the eleven surplus solar days,

Explanation — The lunar and solar years Twelve average lunar months amount to about 354 days, whereas a seasonal solar year is about 365¼ days. The roughly eleven-day difference would move Pesach out of spring if no adjustment were made. The Hebrew calendar solves this by periodically inserting a thirteenth month, so that lunar months remain linked to the solar seasons.
Sefaria connections (editorial): Rambam, Kiddush HaChodesh 6:3 · Deuteronomy 16:1
וְאֵיךְ נַחֲלוֹק הַחֹדֶשׁ לִמְלֵאִים שָׁוִים?!
and how would we divide the months into regular full and deficient months?!
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם שֶׁרָמַז עַל זֶה הָרָאשֵׁי תֵּיבוֹת מִן שִׁשָּׁה סִדְרֵי מִשְׁנָה:
And see there where he hinted at this through the acronym of the Six Orders of the Mishnah:
זְמַן נָקַט (זְרָעִים, מוֹעֵד, נָשִׁים, נְזִיקִין, קָדָשִׁים, טָהֳרוֹת) –
Z-M-N N-Q-T (Zera'im, Mo'ed, Nashim, Nezikin, Kodashim, Tohorot)—

Explanation — Zeman Nakat — mnemonic of the six orders Zeman Nakat is a mnemonic formed from the initials of the six orders of the Mishnah: Zeraim, Moed, Nashim, Nezikin, Kodashim, and Taharot. The words can be read as an instruction to hold fast to the ordering of sacred times. Here it is cited as an allusive argument for the importance of the Oral Torah in determining the calendar, not as a mathematical formula.
Sefaria connections (editorial): Zeraim example: Mishnah Berakhot 1:1 · Moed example: Mishnah Shabbat 1:1
רָצָה לוֹמַר: סֵדֶר זְמַנִּים וּקְבִיעַת חֳדָשִׁים וּמוֹעֲדִים נְקֹט בְּיָדְךָ לְאוֹת וּלְרְאָיָה עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
meaning: grasp in your hand the order of seasons and the setting of months and festivals as a sign and proof of the Oral Torah,
שֶׁכְּמוֹ שֶׁאָנוּ צְרִיכִים לִסְמוֹךְ עֲלֵיהֶם בָּזֶה,
for just as we must rely upon the Sages in this matter,
כֵּן צָרִיךְ לִסְמוֹךְ עֲלֵיהֶם בְּכָל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
so too must we rely upon them regarding the entirety of the Oral Torah.

sections.en: The Challenge to the Received Calendar

p: וְהִנֵּה עַתָּה בָּא הָרַב הַגָּדוֹל מוֹרֵנוּ הָרַב רַבִּי דָּוִד זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה,
And behold now comes the great rabbi, our teacher Rabbi David, of blessed memory,
בַּעַל הַמְּחַבֵּר "חוֹמַת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם", אַב בֵּית דִּין דִּקְהִלַּת קֹדֶשׁ שֶׁרֶשֶׁעב,
author of 'Chomat Yerushalayim', head of the rabbinical court of the holy community of Szereszow,
מְחַבֵּר קוּנְטְרֵס הַלָּז,
author of this pamphlet,
לַחֲלוֹק עָלֵינוּ אֶת הַשָּׁוִים
to subvert established consensus,
וּלְבַלְבֵּל אֶת כָּל עֲדַת יִשְׂרָאֵל
and confound the entire congregation of Israel
בְּעִנְיַן קְבִיעַת הַחֳדָשִׁים וּמוֹעֲדִים הַמָּסוּר לָנוּ מִקַּדְמוֹנֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
regarding the determination of months and festivals transmitted to us by our ancient Sages,
בַּעֲלֵי הַתַּלְמוּד וְכָל הַגְּאוֹנִים וְחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר עַד הַיּוֹם.
the Masters of the Talmud, and all Geonim and sages of Israel down to this day.
וְהוּא חָכָם בְּעֵינָיו לַעֲשׂוֹת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל לְטוֹעִים
And he is wise in his own eyes to declare all of Israel mistaken
בִּדְבָרִים פְּשׁוּטִים וְנוֹדָעִים לְכָל בַּר בֵּי רַב הַקּוֹרֵא חַד יוֹמָא בְּדִבְרֵי רַבֵּינוּ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן מַיְמוֹן בְּהִלְכוֹת קִדּוּשׁ הַחֹדֶשׁ!
in matters elementary and known to any novice student who reads for a single day in the words of Maimonides in Hilchot Kiddush HaChodesh!

Explanation — Hilchot Kiddush HaChodesh This is the section of Rambam’s Mishneh Torah dealing with the sanctification of months, astronomical calculations, witness testimony, intercalation, and the fixed calendar. Because it treats both the earlier sighting-based procedure and later computational rules, its wording is central to the author’s debate about how those two systems relate.
Sefaria connections (editorial): Rambam, Kiddush HaChodesh · Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 2:7
תַּחַת אֲשֶׁר אֲפִילּוּ הָיוּ נִגְלוּ אֵלָיו חֲדָשׁוֹת בְּקוּשְׁיוֹת עַל סֵדֶר קְבִיעוּתֵינוּ,
Whereas even had genuine novel difficulties occurred to him regarding our calendar system,
הָיָה לוֹ לְחַפֵּשׂ וּלְתָרֵץ;
it was his duty to research and resolve them;
וְאִם פִּשְׁפֵּשׁ וְלֹא מָצָא – יִתְלֶה בְּטָעוּת שִׂכְלוֹ,
and had he scrutinized and found no answer, he should have attributed it to the inadequacy of his own intellect,
וְלֹא לַחְשׁוֹד כָּל בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל לְטוֹעִים בְּדָבָר שֶׁהוּא עִיקַּר הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ!
rather than suspecting the entire house of Israel of being in error regarding a matter that is the core of the entire Torah!
הוּא לֹא כֵן עָשָׂה,
He did not act thus,
וּבָא לְהָשִׁיב מִדִּידְהוּ אַדִּידְהוּ וְלִרְדּוֹתֵינוּ תּוֹךְ בֵּיתֵינוּ;
but came to set their sources against themselves and tyrannize us within our own home;
וַאֲשֶׁר לֹא כֵן עָשׂוּ כָּל חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הַקַּדְמוֹנִים וְשֶׁאַחֲרֵיהֶם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה –
which none of the ancient or later sages of Israel ever did,
חִזְּקוּ בְּכָל עֹז סִדְרֵי הַקְּבִיעוּת שֶׁבְּיָדֵינוּ.
who on the contrary reinforced with all might the calendar system in our possession.
וְהָרַב בַּעַל "יְסוֹד עוֹלָם" (מַאֲמָר ג פֶּרֶק יג) הֶאֱרִיךְ וְכָתַב,
And the author of 'Yesod Olam' (Rabbi Isaac Israeli, Discourse 3, Chapter 13) wrote at length,
כִּי קָצְרָה יַד חַכְמֵי הָאֻמּוֹת מִלָּדַעַת שִׁיעוּר הַחֹדֶשׁ בְּצִמְצוּם,
that the hands of gentile astronomers fell short of determining the precise lunar month with exactitude,
וְשֶׁהַמִּדָּה הַמְּדוּיֶּקֶת וְהַנְּכוֹנָה בְּלִי שׁוּם קֵירוּב
and that the exact and correct measure devoid of all approximation
הִיא הַמְּסוּרָה בְּיָדֵינוּ מִפִּי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
is that preserved in our hands from Rabban Gamliel,
שֶׁמְּקֻבָּל מִבֵּית אֲבוֹתָיו הַחֲכָמִים וְהַנְּבִיאִים עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, יְעֻיַּין שָׁם בָּאֹרֶךְ.
received from the house of his ancestors, the Sages and Prophets, peace be upon them, see there at length.
וְשָׁם בְּסִיּוּם הַסֵּפֶר מֵבִיא
And there at the conclusion of the book he cites
שֶׁאֶחָד מֵחַכְמֵי הָעַמִּים גַּם הוּא עִרְעֵר עַל חֶשְׁבּוֹן קְבִיעוּתֵינוּ בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם,
that one of the gentile philosophers likewise challenged our calendar in those days,
וְהוּא הֵשִׁיב לוֹ וְהֶרְאָה לוֹ אֱמֶת חֶשְׁבּוֹנֵנוּ, יְעֻיַּין שָׁם.
and he refuted him, proving the absolute truth of our calculation, see there.
וְנִמְצָא עֵדוּת אֶחָד חָכָם מִן הָאֻמּוֹת הוּבָא בְּסוֹף סֵפֶר "מִקְדַּשׁ מֶלֶךְ" מִסֵּפֶר וַיִּקְרָא
And an endorsement by a gentile astronomer is cited at the end of Sefer Mikdash Melech on Vayikra
שֶׁהוֹדָה לוֹ וְאָמַר,
who conceded to him and declared:
כִּי וַדַּאי הוּא חָכְמַתְכֶם וּבִינַתְכֶם לְעֵינֵי הָעַמִּים, “
Truly this is your wisdom and understanding in the sight of the nations (Deuteronomy 4:6),
כִּי אֵין בְּטֶבַע שֵׂכֶל אֱנוֹשִׁי לְהַשִּׂיג דַּקּוּת הֶפְרֵשׁ חֵלֶק אֶחָד קָטָן כָּל כָּךְ,
for it is not within mortal human intellect to perceive a fraction so minute,
אִם לֹא שֶׁנּוֹדַע שֶׁנִּמְסַר לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי בְּסוֹד הָעִבּוּר כְּדִבְרֵיכֶם,
unless it was transmitted to Moses from Sinai in the secret of the calendar calculation as you say,
וְעָלַי לְהַעֲלוֹת עַל סֵפֶר עַל שֵׁם חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּלֵי, עַד כָּאן.
and it is incumbent upon me to publish this in a book in praise of the Sages of Israel, etc.,” thus far.
גַּם בִּ"יְסוֹד עוֹלָם" (מַאֲמָר ד פֶּרֶק ז) הֵבִיא בְּשֵׁם הֶחָכָם בֶּן צָאעִד בְּסֵפֶר אֶחָד מִסְּפָרָיו,
Also in Yesod Olam (Discourse 4, Chapter 7) he cited in the name of the scholar Sa'id al-Andalusi in one of his works,
כִּי מָצָא בְּיַד הַיְּהוּדִים יְסוֹד מוּסָד וְעִיקָּר אֲמִיתִּי נָכוֹן
that he found in the hands of the Jews a firm foundation and true, accurate calculation
לְמוֹלְדוֹת הַלְּבָנָה וּתְקוּפַת הַחַמָּה, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
for the conjunctions of the moon and the solstices and equinoxes of the sun, see there.

Explanation — Conjunction, equinox, and solstice A lunar conjunction is the astronomical alignment of the sun and moon that marks the calculated new-moon moment; a visible lunar crescent normally appears later. An equinox is a seasonal turning point when day and night are approximately equal; a solstice marks an extreme in the sun’s apparent yearly position. Rabbinic calendar literature calls all four seasonal turning points tekufot.
Sefaria connections (editorial): Rambam, Kiddush HaChodesh 6:3 · Rosh Hashanah 20b

sections.en: The Purpose and Urgency of the Response

p: וְהִנֵּה עַתָּה "מִינֵיהּ וּבֵיהּ אַבָּא שְׁדָא בֵּיהּ נַרְגָּא" (סַנְהֶדְרִין לט עַמּוּד ב) אֲשֶׁר לֹא כַדָּת,
And behold now, from the forest itself comes the axe-handle to fell the trees, contrary to the law,
וְטוֹבָה הָיְתָה לוֹ הַשְּׁתִיקָה וְלִהְיוֹת חָכָם נֶחְשָׁב,
and silence would have been better for him, that he might be counted wise (Proverbs 17:28),
מִלְּדַבֵּר כָּאֵלֶּה וּבַדּוֹרוֹת הַלָּלוּ פֶּן מִי אֵלָיו יִהְיֶה קוֹשֵׁב;
than speaking such contentions, especially in these generations, lest someone listen to him;
כִּי אָזְלַת יַד הַתּוֹרָה בְּדוֹרֵינוּ זֶה,
for the authority of Torah has waned in this generation of ours,
וְיָשִׂישׂוּ כִּי יִמְצְאוּ מִי אֲשֶׁר לְדַת יִשְׂרָאֵל סוֹתֵר,
and heretics will rejoice to find one who undermines the religion of Israel,
וְעַל הַתּוֹרָה יִכְתְּבוּ פְלַסְתֵּר,
writing forgeries against the Torah,
לִסְתּוֹר כָּל חֻקֶּיהָ וְעַל מִצְוֹתֶיהָ לִכְפּוֹת פְּסַכְתֵּר,
to overturn all its statutes and overturn a cover upon its mitzvot,
וּלְהַבְזוֹת כָּל מוֹעֲדֵי אֵל וְלֵאמֹר עַל הֶאָסוּר מוּתָּר,
despising the sacred festivals of God and declaring the forbidden permitted,
וְלַעֲקוֹר כָּל אֱמוּנָתֵנוּ בַּמַּחְתֶּרֶת חוֹתֵר;
undermining our entire faith like a burglar tunneling beneath;
וְהַמַּכְשֵׁלָה הַזֹּאת תַּחַת יָדוֹ בְּתִתּוֹ יָד לַפּוֹשְׁעִים לְנַתֵּר.
and this ruin is under his hand by lending aid to transgressors to break through boundaries.
אִי לָזֹאת, רָאִיתִי לִכְתּוֹב עַל סֵפֶר תְּשׁוּבַת דְּבָרָיו וּמַה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם לִסְתּוֹר,
Wherefore, I have seen fit to record in a book the refutation of his arguments and what must be dismantled in them,
בְּאֹפֶן יֵצֵא כַנֹּגַהּ צִדְקַת חֶשְׁבּוֹנֵנוּ
in order that the truth of our calendar calculation shine forth like radiant light
בִּקְבִיעוּת חֳדָשִׁים וְשָׁנִים פְּשׁוּטוֹת וּמְעֻבָּרוֹת,
in the determination of months, ordinary years, and leap years,
שְׁלֵמִים וַחֲסֵרִים וּסְדוּרִים,
full, deficient, and regular,

Explanation — Shanah shelemah, chaserah, and kesidrah These three classifications describe the length of a fixed-calendar Hebrew year, determined chiefly by the lengths of Cheshvan and Kislev. A deficient year has both months at 29 days; a regular year has 29-day Cheshvan and 30-day Kislev; a complete year has both at 30 days. A common year can thus have 353, 354, or 355 days; a leap year has 383, 384, or 385.
Sefaria connections (editorial): Rambam, Kiddush HaChodesh 8:1
וְאֵין בָּמוֹ נִפְתָּל וְעִקֵּשׁ כַּאֲשֶׁר יְדַמּוּ נְמְהָרִים.
there being nothing perverse or crooked within them as hasty individuals imagine.
וְהִנְנִי לְהָשִׁיב עַל דְּבָרָיו, אֶת נִסִּי אָרִים,
And behold I step forward to reply to his words, raising my banner,
וְלֹא אֵבוֹשׁ גַּם כִּי אֲדַבֵּר נֶגֶד זְקֵנִים וְשָׂרִים,
and will not be ashamed even when addressing elders and dignitaries,
כִּי אַךְ לְחַזֵּק דַּת יְשֻׁרוּן וַלַּהֲקִימָהּ עַל תִּלָּהּ הַדְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים.
for solely to fortify the faith of Yeshurun and restore it upon its foundation are these words spoken.
צוּרִי אֶחֱסֶה בּוֹ, כִּי הוּא מָגִנִּי וְקֶרֶן יִשְׁעִי לָעַד וּלְדוֹר דּוֹרִים.
In my Rock do I take refuge, for He is my shield and the horn of my salvation forever and for all generations.
וְהִנֵּה כָּתַבְתִּי לְהָשִׁיב גַּם עַל דְּבָרָיו שֶׁאֵינָם נוֹגְעִים לְגוּף הָעִנְיָן שֶׁרָצָה בוֹ לְחַדֵּשׁ,
And behold, I have written to reply even to his comments that do not bear directly upon the thesis he wished to innovate,
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁעָשׂוּ חֲכָמִים זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה לַחֲנַנְיָה חֲנִינָא בֶּן אֲחִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
as our Sages did to Chananyah the nephew of Rabbi Yehoshua,
שֶׁעִבֵּר שָׁנִים וְקָבַע חֳדָשִׁים בְּחוּץ לָאָרֶץ,
who intercalated years and established months outside the Land of Israel,

Explanation — Ibbur ha-shanah — adding a leap month Intercalation of a year means adding an extra month, traditionally a second Adar, in order to preserve the festivals in their proper seasons. It must not be confused with making an individual month full by assigning it a thirtieth day; both procedures are sometimes called intercalation in English translations. Context determines whether the discussion concerns the year or one month.
Sefaria connections (editorial): Rambam, Kiddush HaChodesh 4:1 · Sanhedrin 11b
כִּדְאִיתָא בְּשִׁילְהֵי בְּרָכוֹת (סג עַמּוּד א), כִּי הֵיכֵי דְּלָא נִגְרְרוּ עָלְמָא אַבַּתְרֵיהּ, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
as brought at the end of Berakhot (63a), so that the public would not be drawn after him, see there.
וּלְפִי שֶׁהָרַב הַנִּזְכָּר בַּעַל הַקּוּנְטְרֵס קָרָא קוּנְטְרֵסוֹ "מְגִילַּת טַעֲנוֹת",
And because the aforementioned author titled his pamphlet 'Megillat Ta'anot',
רָאִיתִי אֲנִי לִקְרוֹא שֵׁם קוּנְטְרֵס זֶה תְּשׁוּבַת דְּבָרָיו "מֵשִׁיב הַטַּעֲנָה",
I have seen fit to title this pamphlet refuting his arguments 'Meishiv HaTa'anah',
וְהִנְנִי מַתְחִיל וְאוֹמֵר:
and behold I begin, saying:

sections.en: The Yerushalmi and Sanctification by Witnesses

p: כָּתַב בַּעַל הַקּוּנְטְרֵס: יְרוּשַׁלְמִי שִׁילְהֵי סֻכָּה וְכוּלֵי.
The author of the pamphlet wrote: Jerusalem Talmud, end of Sukkah, etc.
אָמַר הַכּוֹתֵב: רָאִיתִי לְהַקְדִּים לָזֶה לְבָאֵר עִנְיַן קְבִיעוּת הַחֳדָשִׁים עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה,
The writer says: I have seen fit to preface this by clarifying the determination of months according to the Torah,
וְאוֹמֵר שֶׁדָּבָר בָּרוּר הוּא וּמְבוֹאָר בַּתַּלְמוּד בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת
and I say that it is a clear matter, explicated in the Talmud in multiple places
מִמַּסֶּכֶת רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְסַנְהֶדְרִין וַעֲרָכִין וְזוּלָתָם:
in Tractate Rosh Hashanah, Sanhedrin, Arachin, and elsewhere:
כִּי עִיקַּר קְבִיעוּת חֳדָשִׁים בִּזְמַן שֶׁהָיוּ קוֹבְעִים עַל פִּי הָרְאִיָּה
that the primary establishment of months when they determined via sighting
הָיָה תָּלוּי בָּרְאִיָּה וּבְהַעֲדָאַת הָעֵדִים,
was dependent upon visual sighting and the formal testimony of witnesses,

Explanation — Edut ha-chodesh — testimony concerning the moon In the earlier court-based system, witnesses who saw the new crescent testified before an authorized court, which could proclaim the new month. This is different from calculating the mean lunar conjunction. A calculation could guide the court, but the debate here asks whether testimony or fixed arithmetic determined the legally operative date in the period under discussion.
Sefaria connections (editorial): Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 2:6 · Rambam, Kiddush HaChodesh 2:1
וְלֹא בַּחֶשְׁבּוֹן שֶׁבְּיָדֵינוּ;
and not upon the fixed calendar calculation in our hands;
וַאֲפִילּוּ הָיָה עַל פִּי חֶשְׁבּוֹנֵנוּ רָאוּי לִהְיוֹת רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ בִּשְׁלֹשִׁים,
and even if according to our calculation it was due to be Rosh Chodesh on day thirty,
אִם לֹא בָּאוּ עֵדִים וְלֹא הֵעִידוּ עַל הָרְאִיָּה
if witnesses did not arrive and testify to the sighting,
לֹא הָיוּ קוֹבְעִים רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ אֶלָּא בְּיוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים וְאֶחָד,
they would not establish Rosh Chodesh until day thirty-one,
וְכֵן לְהֵיפֶךְ.
and likewise the reverse.
וְדָבָר זֶה פָּשׁוּט אֵצֶל כָּל הַקַּדְמוֹנִים.
And this principle is elementary and clear to all ancient authorities.

sections.en: Rav Saadia Gaon and the Fixed Calendar

p: זוּלַת בְּסֵפֶר "יְסוֹד עוֹלָם" (מַאֲמָר ד פֶּרֶק ו) הֵבִיא בְּשֵׁם רַבֵּינוּ סְעַדְיָה גָּאוֹן זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
Except that in Sefer Yesod Olam (Discourse 4, Chapter 6) he cited in the name of Rabbeinu Saadia Gaon, of blessed memory,
שֶׁאָמַר כִּי מֵעוֹלָם, וַאֲפִילּוּ כְּשֶׁהָיָה הַבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים,
who held that never, even when the Holy Temple was standing,
לֹא הָיוּ קוֹבְעִים הַחֳדָשִׁים אֶלָּא עַל פִּי חֶשְׁבּוֹן שֶׁבְּיָדֵינוּ
did they establish months except according to the fixed calculation in our hands
מֵעִבּוּר הַשָּׁנִים בַּמַּחֲזוֹר עַל פִּי סֵדֶר גּוּחַֽ אֲדְזַ"ט (שָׁנִים ג, ו, ח, יא, יד, יז, יט),
intercalating leap years in the nineteen-year cycle according to the sequence GuCh ADZaT (years 3, 6, 8, 11, 14, 17, 19),

Explanation — GuCh ADZaT — the seven leap years GuCh ADZaT is a memory aid for the leap-year positions in each nineteen-year Hebrew-calendar cycle. The Hebrew letters represent the numbers 3, 6, 8, 11, 14, 17, and 19. Those seven years each contain thirteen months; the remaining twelve years contain twelve. Thus the cycle has 235 lunar months in all. This mnemonic identifies year numbers, not days of the week.
Sefaria connections (editorial): Rambam, Kiddush HaChodesh 6:10
וּדְחִיַּית קְבוּעַ רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה מִימֵי אֲדּ"וּ (אֶחָד, דַּלֶּת, וָאו)
and the postponement of Rosh Hashanah from occurring on Sunday, Wednesday, or Friday (ADU),

Explanation — Lo ADU Rosh — the weekday exclusion ADU is the Hebrew-letter abbreviation aleph–dalet–vav, whose numerical values are 1, 4, and 6: Sunday, Wednesday, and Friday. Lo ADU Rosh means that, in the fixed Hebrew calendar, the first day of Rosh Hashanah cannot fall on any of those days. If its computed date would do so, it is postponed. Among the practical consequences are avoiding Yom Kippur immediately adjacent to Shabbat and Hoshana Rabbah on Shabbat. See Rambam, Kiddush HaChodesh 7:1, 7:7.
Sefaria connections (editorial): Rambam, Kiddush HaChodesh 7:1
וּשְׁאָר דְּחִיַּית הַקְּבִיעוּת וְכָל עִנְיְנֵי הָעִבּוּר שֶׁבְּיָדֵינוּ,
and the other calendar postponements and intercalary rules in our possession,

Explanation — Dechiyot — calendar postponement rules Dechiyot are rules that defer the calendrical date of Rosh Hashanah from the raw calculation of the Tishrei molad. Besides Lo ADU, the traditional rules include molad zaken, a molad at or after noon; GaTaRaD, Tuesday at or after 9 hours 204 parts in a common year; and BeTuTaKPaT, Monday at or after 15 hours 589 parts in a year following a leap year. The last two guard against invalid year lengths. The author is examining how ancient these rules are, not merely how to apply them today.
Sefaria connections (editorial): Rambam, Kiddush HaChodesh 7:1–2 · Rambam, Kiddush HaChodesh 7:7
שֶׁהַכֹּל נִמְסַר לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִפִּי הַגְּבוּרָה,
all of which were transmitted to Moses our teacher directly from the Almighty,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּמְסַר לוֹ עִנְיַן הַתְּפִלִּין וְהִלְכוֹתֵיהֶם;
just as the mitzvah of tefillin and its laws were transmitted to him;
וּמַה שֶּׁנֶּזְכַּר בַּגְּמָרָא מִן הָרְאִיָּה
and what is mentioned in the Gemara regarding visual sighting
הוּא מִתַּקָּנַת בְּנֵי דּוֹרוֹ וּבֵית דִּינוֹ שֶׁל אַנְטִיגְנוֹס אִישׁ סוֹכוֹ,
was an enactment of the generation and court of Antignos of Sokho,
שֶׁהִתְקִינוּ רְאִיַּת הַלְּבָנָה בְּחִידּוּשָׁהּ כְּדֵי לְהַרְאוֹת אֲמִיתַּת הַדָּבָר,
who instituted visual sighting of the moon's renewal to demonstrate empirical proof,
וּלְבַטֵּל דִּבְרֵי צָדוֹק וּבַיְתוֹס שֶׁהָיוּ טוֹעֲנִים נֶגֶד הַחֲכָמִים בְּמִדַּת זְמַן הַחֹדֶשׁ;
and refute the claims of Zadok and Boethus who disputed the Sages regarding the month's duration;
אֲבָל מֵעוֹלָם לֹא קָבְעוּ הַחֹדֶשׁ אֶלָּא עַל פִּי הַחֶשְׁבּוֹן שֶׁבְּיָדֵינוּ;
yet never did they establish the month except according to the calculation in our hands;
וּמַה שֶּׁנִּמְצָא בַּגְּמָרָא פִּלְפּוּלִים וַהֲלָכוֹת בִּקְבִיעוּת שֶׁאֵינָם בְּאֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת עַל פִּי חֶשְׁבּוֹנֵנוּ
and whatever Talmudic debates and rulings assume calendar occurrences impossible under our calculation,
כְּעִנְיַן כִּבְשֵׂי עֲצֶרֶת אֵין דּוֹחֶה שַׁבָּת וְהַדּוֹמֶה,
such as the Pentecost sheep not overriding Shabbat and the like,
לֹא נֶאֶמְרוּ אֶלָּא לְפַלְפֵּל לַתַּלְמִידִים שֶׁיֵּדְעוּ אֵיךְ הַדִּין אִילּוּ הָיָה נִמְצָא,
were stated solely for theoretical academic training so students know the law hypothetically,
אֵלּוּ תּוֹרֶף דְּבָרָיו זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה.
such is the essence of his words, of blessed memory.
וּכְבָר הֵשִׁיב עֲלֵיהֶם הָרַב הַמְּחַבֵּר
And the author of Yesod Olam already refuted this,
וּמַה שֶּׁהֵבִיא בְּשֵׁם רַבֵּינוּ יִצְחָק בֶּן רַבִּי בָּרוּךְ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
citing in the name of Rabbeinu Yitzchak ben Rabbi Baruch
מֵחֲבִילוֹת חֲבִילוֹת שֶׁל סוּגְיוֹת הַמּוֹרִים הֵיפֶךְ דַּעְתּוֹ;
multitudes of Talmudic treatises proving the opposite of Saadia Gaon's view;
וְיֵשׁ לְהוֹסִיף עֲלֵיהֶם כָּהֵנָּה וְכָהֵנָּה.
and one may add to them manifold further proofs.
וּמִכְּלָלָם מַה שֶּׁהוּא מִן הַתֵּימַהּ מִדָּבָר הַפָּשׁוּט לַכֹּל,
Among them is the striking difficulty from that which is obvious to everyone:
מַה שֶּׁאָנוּ עוֹשִׂים שְׁנֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים שֶׁל גָּלֻיּוֹת,
why we observe the second festival day of the Diaspora,

Explanation — Yom Tov Sheni shel Galuyot The second festival day observed in the Diaspora is traditionally associated with an era when distant communities could not immediately learn which day the court in the Land of Israel had declared Rosh Chodesh. This historical uncertainty is part of the author’s evidence that court testimony once mattered. Rosh Hashanah’s two-day observance has its own history and is discussed separately in the passage.
Sefaria connections (editorial): Beitzah 4b · Rosh Hashanah 18a
שֶׁהוּא מִנְהַג אֲבוֹתֵינוּ בְּיָדֵינוּ
which is an ancestral custom preserved in our hands,
שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ יוֹדְעִים בְּעִבּוּרוֹ שֶׁל חֹדֶשׁ בְּאֵיזֶה יוֹם קָבְעוּ בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל;
because they did not know on which day the court in the Land of Israel sanctified the month;
וְאִם לֹא קָבְעוּ אֶלָּא עַל פִּי חֶשְׁבּוֹן,
and if they never determined except by fixed calculation,
הֲלֹא נָקֵל הָיָה לָהֶם לָדַעַת כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָנוּ יוֹדְעִים עַכְשָׁיו?!
would it not have been easy for them to know in advance just as we know today?!
וְכִי תֵימָא אַנְשֵׁי חוּצָה לָאָרֶץ לֹא הָיוּ אָז בְּנֵי תוֹרָה וְלֹא יָדְעוּ חֶשְׁבּוֹן זֶה,
And should you claim Diaspora Jews were not scholars and were ignorant of this calculation,
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּגִטִּין (ב עַמּוּד ב) לְעִנְיַן "לִשְׁמָהּ" –
as in the first chapter of Gittin (2b) regarding the phrase lishmah—
עֲדַיִן מַה נֹּאמַר עַל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
still what shall we say concerning Rosh Hashanah,
שֶׁעוֹשִׂים גַּם בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל שְׁנֵי יָמִים מִשּׁוּם מִנְהַג אֲבוֹתֵינוּ
which they observe for two days even in the Land of Israel due to ancestral custom,
שֶׁמָּא בָּאוּ עֵדִים מִן הַמִּנְחָה וּלְמַעְלָה?!
lest witnesses arrive from Minchah onward?!
וְאַמַּאי הָיוּ בְּנֵי אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהָיוּ בְּנֵי תוֹרָה עוֹשִׂים שְׁנֵי יָמִים
Why would the scholars of the Land of Israel observe two days
וְלֹא יָדְעוּ עַל פִּי חֶשְׁבּוֹן יוֹם הַקְּבִיעוּת?!
and fail to determine the day of the New Year by calculation?!
וְרַבֵּינוּ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן מַיְמוֹן (פֶּרֶק יא מֵהִלְכוֹת קִדּוּשׁ הַחֹדֶשׁ הֲלָכָה ד) כָּתַב:
And Maimonides wrote (Hilchot Kiddush HaChodesh 11:4):
שֶׁזֶּה הַחֶשְׁבּוֹן שֶׁאָנוּ מְחַשְּׁבִין בּוֹ הַיּוֹם
that this calendar calculation we calculate today,
אֲפִילּוּ תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן מַגִּיעִים עַד סוֹפוֹ בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה וְאַרְבָּעָה יָמִים;
even schoolchildren can master completely in three or four days;
וְלָמָּה לֹא יְדָעוּהוּ הֵם וְעָשׂוּ שְׁנֵי יָמִים רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה עַל מַגָּן?!
why then would they be ignorant of it and keep two days of Rosh Hashanah in vain?!
אֶלָּא וַדַּאי שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה קְבִיעָתָם אָז אֶלָּא עַל פִּי עֵדֵי הָרְאִיָּה בִּלְבַד וְלֹא בְּחֶשְׁבּוֹנֵנוּ.
Rather, certainly their determination then depended exclusively upon witnesses of visual sighting and not upon our calculation. (
וְלִפְעָמִים מְאַיְּימִין עַל הָעֵדִים, אֲבָל צָרִיךְ לָזֶה תְּנָאִים יְדוּעִים, (
And at times the court intimidated witnesses, but this required specific conditions,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהֶאֱרַכְנוּ בָּזֶה בִּמְקוֹמוֹ וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ).
as we elaborated in its place, and this is not the place for it).

p: וּמָצָאתִי לְרַבֵּינוּ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן מַיְמוֹן זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה בְּפֵירוּשׁ הַמִּשְׁנָיוֹת

and asserts that the Jewish religion is not founded on sighting the moon but solely on calculation,
וְהוּא מַאֲמִין וְכוּלֵי", יְעֻיַּין שָׁם אֹרֶךְ דְּבָרָיו.
while he believes, etc.”, see there at length.
יֵרָאֶה שֶׁנִּתְכַּוֵּין בָּזֶה גַּם כֵּן לְרַב סְעַדְיָה גָּאוֹן זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה,
It appears that he aimed this critique likewise at Rav Saadia Gaon,

dismissing his thesis firmly on account of the manifest clarity and truth of the matter.

However, regarding the postponements of Rosh Hashanah from occurring on days ADU (Sunday, Wednesday, Friday),

that even when establishing via visual sighting they would postpone from its day

and intimidate witnesses,
כִּדְאִיתָא (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כ עַמּוּד א):
as brought in Rosh Hashanah (20a):
כִּי אֲתָא עוּלָּא אָמַר: עַבְּרוּהָ לֶאֱלוּל;
When Ulla arrived he said: They intercalated Elul (making it 30 days);

Explanation — Ibbur ha-chodesh — making a month full When the Gemara says that the court intercalated Elul, the immediate issue is whether Elul was allowed to run for thirty days instead of ending after twenty-nine. That postpones the next month’s first day. It is not the same as adding a second Adar to the year. Much of the ensuing argument turns on whether the court could lengthen a month for a practical need.

that Ulla instituted this postponement of Rosh Hashanah due to herbs and the dead.

and this explains what the Gemara states in Rosh Hashanah (ibid.):

because Rabbi Yochanan was among the enactors of the ordinance, belonging to Rabbi's court, thus far.

p: אֲבָל אֵין זֶה מוּכְרָח,
However, this is not compelling,
וְלֹא בְּמַשְׁמָע מִלְּשׁוֹן הַגְּמָרָא שֶׁיִּהְיֶה זֶה תַּקָּנָה נִתְחַדְּשָׁה בִּימֵי עוּלָּא אוֹ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן;
nor is it implied from the Gemara that this was an innovation of Ulla or Rabbi Yochanan;
וְעוּלָּא דְּאָמַר "טִיבוּתָא עֲבַדוּ בַּהֲדַיְיהוּ" –
and Ulla saying 'a favor they did for them'—
הַיְינוּ בְּמַה שֶּׁיְּעַבְּרוּהוּ עָשׂוּ לָהֶם טִיבוּתָא,
means that in that specific instance of intercalating they did them a favor,

not that it constituted a newly minted decree.
וּבְפֶרֶק "תָּמִיד נִשְׁחָט" (פְּסָחִים נח עַמּוּד ב):
And in the chapter 'Tamid Nishchat' (Pesachim 58b):
תָּנֵי: עֶרֶב פֶּסַח שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשֵׁנִי בְּשַׁבָּת;
It was taught: The fourteenth of Nisan that fell on Monday;
וּפֵירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י (רַבֵּינוּ שְׁלֹמֹה יִצְחָקִי):
and Rashi explained:
אִית דְּאָמַר דְּנָקַט בְּשֵׁנִי בְּשַׁבָּת
some say it formulated on Monday
מִשּׁוּם דְּהוּא יוֹמָא קַמָּא דַּחֲזֵי לְאַרְבֵּיסַר,
because Monday is the earliest day fit for the fourteenth,
דְּחַד בְּשַׁבְּתָא לָא חֲזֵי לְאַרְבֵּיסַר מִשּׁוּם דְּ"לֹא בַּדּ"וּ פֶּסַח" (בֵּית, דַּלֶּת, וָאו),
since Sunday cannot be the fourteenth because Passover never begins on BaDU (Monday, Wednesday, Friday),

Explanation — Lo BaDU Pesach BaDU is bet–dalet–vav, with numerical values 2, 4, and 6: Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Lo BaDU Pesach means that under the fixed calendar the first day of Pesach never falls on those weekdays. It is a different mnemonic from Lo ADU Rosh: BaDU concerns Pesach; ADU concerns Rosh Hashanah. The passage asks whether such weekday exclusions governed the older sighting-based calendar as well.
