p: וְאָמְנָם מַה שֶּׁאוֹמֵר אֲנִי:
However, that which I submit is:
כִּי הֲלֹא יָדוּעַ מַה שֶּׁהִתְפָּאֵר שְׁמוּאֵל:
for behold it is known that Shmuel declared: "
נְהִירִין לִי שְׁבִילֵי דִּרְקִיעָא כִּשְׁבִילֵי דִּנְהַרְדְּעָא" כִּדְאִיתָא בִּבְרָכוֹת (נח עַמּוּד ב), “
The pathways of heaven are as luminous to me as the streets of Nehardea” (Berakhot 58b),
וּבְוַדַּאי כָּל רָז לֹא אָנֵיס לֵיהּ מִמִּדַּת תְּקוּפַת הַחַמָּה.
and certainly no astronomical secret regarding the solar cycle was concealed from him.
וְכֵן בְּ"יְסוֹד עוֹלָם" (מַאֲמָר ד פֶּרֶק יא)
And likewise in Yesod Olam (Discourse 4, chapter 11)
הֵבִיא מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ: "תְּקוּפַת שְׁמוּאֵל בְּפַרְהֶסְיָא וּתְקוּפַת רַב אַדָּא בְּצִנְעָא",
he cited the teaching: “Shmuel's equinox in public, Rav Adda's equinox in private,”

Explanation — Tekufah ba-rabbim and ba-lachash “In public” and “in private” distinguish the simpler tekufah used for widely practiced communal calculations from a more technical reckoning discussed among specialists. The writer later offers a homiletic interpretation of this pairing as public action versus inward thought. That spiritual interpretation should be kept separate from the practical numerical distinction.
Sefaria connections (editorial): Rambam, Kiddush HaChodesh 9–10
וְכָתַב שֶׁהוּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה מִנְהַג הַחֲכָמִים מִקֶּדֶם לְהַסְתִּיר עִנְיְנֵי הַחָכְמוֹת וְכוּלֵי;
writing that ancient sages made a practice of concealing esoteric sciences, etc.;
מְבוֹאָר שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת.
demonstrating that both traditions are authentic truth.
וְכָתַב: וּשְׁמוּאֵל שֶׁעָשָׂה זְמַן הַשָּׁנָה עוֹדֵף עַל זְמַנָּהּ הַמְּדוּיָּק לָהּ,
And he wrote: Shmuel rounding the solar year slightly longer than its exact astronomical value
אֵינוֹ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּתְעַלֵּם מִמֶּנּוּ זֶה,
was not because this precision was unknown to him,
אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁרָצָה לְהָקֵל חֶשְׁבּוֹן הַתְּקוּפוֹת וְכוּלֵי, יְעֻיַּין שָׁם.
but because he wished to simplify calculation for the masses, see there.
וּלְפִיכָךְ יָפֶה כָּתַב רַבֵּינוּ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן מַיְמוֹן
Therefore Maimonides formulated it exquisitely,
שֶׁבִּזְמַן בֵּית דִּין הַגָּדוֹל סָמְכוּ עַל תְּקוּפַת דְּרַב אַדָּא,
that during the era of the Great Sanhedrin they relied upon Rav Adda's equinox,
לְפִי שֶׁחֶשְׁבּוֹן הָרְאִיָּה אֵינוֹ מָסוּר אֶלָּא לְבֵית דִּין בִּלְבַד,
because the sighting calculations were entrusted exclusively to the high court,
וּבֵית דִּין זְרִיזִים הֵם לְדַיֵּיק בַּחֶשְׁבּוֹן עַל דֶּרֶךְ הַדִּיּוּק בְּצִמְצוּם וְכִיוּוּן גָּמוּר;
and the court is diligent to compute with rigorous mathematical precision;
אֲבָל חֶשְׁבּוֹן תְּקוּפוֹת הַמָּסוּר לַכֹּל הוּא כִּדְשְׁמוּאֵל,
whereas the public calendar equinox entrusted to all of Israel follows Shmuel,
לִהְיוֹת הַחֶשְׁבּוֹן נָקֵל וְקָרוֹב לַעֲשׂוֹתוֹ:
to render the reckoning accessible and easy to execute:
וּלְפִי זֶה אֲנִי אוֹמֵר,
And based upon this principle I state,
עַל הַדֶּרֶךְ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּחִדּוּשַׁי לְיוֹרֶה דֵּעָה (סִימָן ל),
along the lines of what I recorded in my novellae to Yoreh De'ah (sec. 30),
דְּכָתַב שָׁם הַמְּחַבֵּר (סָעִיף קָטָן ב):
where the Shulchan Aruch writes (par. 2): "
כְּסֶלַע שֶׁהִיא שְׁלִישׁ טֶפַח", עַיֵּין שָׁם; “
like a sela coin which is a third of a handbreadth,” see there;
וְהִקְשָׁה הַשַּׁ"ךְ (שִׂפְתֵי כֹהֵן סָעִיף קָטָן ה):
and the Shach objects (subparagraph 5):
הָא כָּתְבוּ הַתּוֹסָפוֹת (עֵירוּבִין יד עַמּוּד א דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "וְהָאִיכָּא")
Behold Tosafot in Eruvin (14a s.v. "VeHaIka")
וְרַבֵּינוּ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן מַיְמוֹן (בְּפֵירוּשׁ הַמִּשְׁנָה שָׁם יג עַמּוּד ב)
and Maimonides in his commentary on the Mishnah (13b)
שֶׁהַכְּלָל שֶׁכָּל מַה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ בְּרָחְבּוֹ טֶפַח יֵשׁ בְּהֶקֵּיפוֹ שְׁלוֹשָׁה טְפָחִים
that the rule 'whatever has a width of one handbreadth has a circumference of three handbreadths'
אֵינוֹ מְדוּקְדָּק לְפִי חַכְמֵי הַמִּדּוֹת
is not mathematically exact according to geometers,
אֶלָּא הוּא כְּדֵי שְׁלוֹשָׁה טְפָחִים וּשְׁבִיעִית בְּקֵירוּב (פַּאי = 3.14159);
being approximately three and one-seventh handbreadths (pi ≈ 22/7);

Explanation — The approximation of pi in halachic measures The talmudic rule relating a circle’s circumference to its diameter often uses the simplified ratio 3:1. A more precise mathematical value is approximately 3.14159, sometimes estimated as 22/7. Here the author uses the contrast to discuss when a legal measurement follows an established conventional rule rather than the most mathematically exact value.
Sefaria connections (editorial): Eruvin 14a · Sukkah 8a
וְאִם כֵּן אֵין הַסֶּלַע אֶלָּא פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלִישׁ טֶפַח,
and if so the sela's diameter is less than a third of a handbreadth,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁהֶקֵּף הַסֶּלַע טֶפַח,
since the sela's circumference is one handbreadth,
וְאַף בְּפָחוֹת רָאוּי שֶׁיִּטָּרֵף, עַיֵּין שָׁם;
and even with a smaller puncture the animal should be rendered treifah, see there;
וְנִמְשְׁכוּ אַחֲרָיו הָרַב "תְּבוּאוֹת שׁוֹר" וְהָרַב "הַפְּלֵתִי" שָׁם, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
and the Tevu'ot Shor and the Pleti followed his reasoning, see there.
וַאֲנִי כָּתַבְתִּי שָׁם כִּי יֵשׁ לִתְמוֹהַּ עֲלֵיהֶם,
And I wrote there that it is astonishing of them,
כִּי הֲלֹא מְבוֹאָר בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּעֵירוּבִין (יד עַמּוּד א)
for behold it is explicitly articulated in the first chapter of Eruvin (14a)
שֶׁעַל דֶּרֶךְ הַדִּיּוּק אִיתְּמַר הַאי כְּלָלָא וְשֶׁהוּא מְכֻוָּון הֵיטֵב,
that this proportion was stated as a precise halakhic axiom and is thoroughly exact,
וְכֵן כָּתְבוּ הַתּוֹסָפוֹת שָׁם דְּמוּכָח כֵּן מִגְּמָרָא (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא יד עַמּוּד ב),
and Tosafot wrote there that this is proven from Bava Batra (14b),
אֶלָּא שֶׁהֵם כָּתְבוּ: וְקָשֶׁה שֶׁאֵין הַחֶשְׁבּוֹן מְכֻוָּון לְפִי חַכְמֵי הַמִּדּוֹת.
save that they noted: it is difficult that it does not match geometric science.
וְלֹא בִּשְׁבִיל הַקּוּשְׁיָא שֶׁלֹּא יָדְעוּ לְתָרֵץ
Yet not on account of a mathematical difficulty they could not resolve
נִדְחֶה דִּבְרֵי גְּמָרָא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם מֵהֲלָכָה!
shall we ever cast aside the words of the Talmud from halakhic authority, Heaven forbid!

sections.en: Tashbetz and the Limits of Mathematical Exactitude

p: וְהֵבֵאתִי שָׁם דִּבְרֵי הַתַּשְׁבֵּ"ץ (רַבֵּינוּ שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן צֶמַח דּוּרָאן, חֵלֶק א סִימָן קסה)
And I cited there the words of the Tashbetz (Part I, responsum 165)
הֱשִׁיב לְאֶחָד מֵחַכְמֵי הַמִּדּוֹת וְהַהַנְדָּסָה
who replied to one of the geometric and mathematical scholars
שֶׁכָּתַב אֵלָיו כִּי אֵין הַחֶשְׁבּוֹן וְהַכְּלָל שֶׁבַּגְּמָרָא הַנִּזְכָּר נֶאֱמַר עַל צַד הַדִּיּוּק
who had written to him that the Talmudic mathematical rule was not stated with exactitude,
וְשֶׁלְּחוּמְרָא לָא דָּקּוּ.
and that for strict stringency they did not compute precisely.
וֶהֱשִׁיבוֹ דְּזֶה לֵיתָא,
And he refuted him that this is incorrect,
מֵהַהוּא דְּקוֹרָה הָתָם בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּעֵירוּבִין שֶׁהוּא לְהָקֵל;
from the case of the crossbeam in the first chapter of Eruvin where it functions leniently;
וְאִי מִשּׁוּם דְּאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מִדְּרַבָּנָן –
and if one argues it is merely rabbinic—
לֹא מָצִינוּ קוּלָּא בִּדְרַבָּנָן אֶלָּא בִּסְפֵיקָא, לֹא לְעִנְיַן הַשִּׁיעוּר,
we never find leniency in rabbinic law except in matters of doubt, not regarding defined measurements,
וּכְעִנְיָן שֶׁאָמְרוּ (חֻלִּין צח עַמּוּד א): "לָא תְּזַלְזֵל בְּשִׁיעוּרָא דְּרַבָּנָן".
as they stated (Chullin 98a): 'Do not treat rabbinic measurements lightly.'
וְעוֹד הוֹכִיחַ שֶׁסָּמְכוּ עָלָיו אַף לְהָקֵל
Furthermore he proved that they relied upon it even leniently
מִפֶּרֶק יב דְּאָהֳלוֹת (מִשְׁנָה ו-ז)
from chapter 12 of Ohalot (mishnayot 6–7)
בְּדֶרֶךְ מַה נַּפְשָׁךְ:
by way of alternative logic:
אִם לְטַמֵּא – קוּלָּא מִשּׁוּם הֶפְסֵד טָהֳרוֹת, אוֹ לְטַהֵר, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
if to declare impure—it is a leniency to prevent loss of pure items, or to declare pure, see there. (
וּקְצָת חִידּוּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיא מִדִּבְרֵי הַגְּמָרָא דְּעֵירוּבִין הַנִּזְכָּר (
And it is somewhat surprising that he did not cite the Gemara in Eruvin mentioned earlier
וּמִדִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹסָפוֹת שָׁם דִּמְבוֹאָר דְּהַחֶשְׁבּוֹן בְּדִיּוּק גָּמוּר;
and Tosafot there wherein it is clear that the calculation is absolute precision;
מִיהוּ רָאִיתִי שָׁם בִּתְחִלַּת הַסִּימָן נִרְאֶה שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ נוּסְחָא אַחֶרֶת בְּדִבְרֵי הַתּוֹסָפוֹת, עַיֵּין שָׁם).
however I saw at the beginning of that responsum that he seemingly had a variant textual reading in Tosafot, see there).
וּמַסִּיק וְכָתַב:
And he concludes and writes: "
אֶלָּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָנוּ לֵאמֹר שֶׁקַּבָּלָתָן כָּךְ הָיְתָה “
Rather we must maintain that their tradition was thus:
לָלֶכֶת בְּכָל הַחֶשְׁבּוֹנוֹת שֶׁבְּדִינֵי הַתּוֹרָה עַל פִּי הַדְּרָכִים הָאֵלּוּ,
to proceed in all calculations across Torah jurisprudence according to these methods,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם קֵירוּב כְּאִלּוּ מְדוּקְדָּקִים,
even though they contain an approximation, as though they were mathematically exact;
וְכָךְ הָיְתָה הֲלָכָה לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי וְכוּלֵי",
and thus was the Halakhah transmitted to Moses from Sinai, etc.”
יְעֻיַּין שָׁם שֶׁכָּתַב עוֹד דֶּרֶךְ אַחֵר,
see there where he offers another explanation,
אֲבָל זֶהוּ הָעִיקָּר בְּוַדַּאי;
but this is certainly the primary bedrock;
וְיִשַּׁבְתִּי עַל פִּי זֶה דִּבְרֵי הַמְּחַבֵּר שָׁם בְּיוֹרֶה דֵּעָה, עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּחִדּוּשַׁי בַּאֲרִיכוּת:
and I reconciled through this the Shulchan Aruch in Yoreh De'ah, see my novellae at length:
וְהִנֵּה כְּמוֹ כֵן אֲנִי אוֹמֵר כָּאן,
And behold likewise I assert here,
שֶׁקַּבָּלָתָם כָּךְ הָיְתָה:
that their tradition was thus:
שֶׁבְּכָל עִנְיָנִים הַמִּצְטָרְכִים אֶל כָּל עֲדַת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
that in all affairs required by the entire congregation of Israel,
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְכָל אֶחָד לַחְשׁוֹב בְּדִיּוּק כִּתְקוּפַת דְּרַב אַדָּא,
where it is impossible for every layman to compute rigorously according to Rav Adda's equinox,
יִהְיֶה הַחֶשְׁבּוֹן עַל פִּי תְּקוּפַת שְׁמוּאֵל,
the public reckoning shall proceed according to Shmuel's equinox,
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָהּ אֶלָּא עַל צַד הַקֵּירוּב – כְּאִלּוּ הָיְתָה מְדוּיֶּקֶת בְּכִיוּוּן גָּמוּר.
and even though it is an approximation—treated as if it were fully aligned with absolute precision.
וַהֲרֵי מִי שֶׁבָּרָא אֶת הַחַמָּה וְיִסַּד הַתְּקוּפוֹת,
For He Who created the sun and established the equinoxes,
הוּא שֶׁצִּיוָּוה עָלֵינוּ שֶׁאֲנַחְנוּ לֹא נִמְנֶה הַתְּקוּפוֹת כֵּן כְּמוֹ שֶׁהֵם בְּדִיּוּק,
is the One Who commanded us that we should not reckon the equinoxes precisely as they are physically,
אֶלָּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁהֵם עַל דֶּרֶךְ הַקֵּירוּב וַעֲלֵיהֶם נִסְמוֹךְ.
but rather according to this accessible approximation, and upon it we rely.
וּלְפִיכָךְ עַל זֶה אָנוּ סוֹמְכִין לְבָרֵךְ "בָּרוּךְ עֹשֵׂה מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית"
Therefore upon this we rely to recite 'Blessed is the Author of Creation'
בִּתְחִלַּת כ"ח (עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁמוֹנֶה) לַחַמָּה,
at the beginning of the 28-year solar cycle,
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ אָז זְמַן הַתְּקוּפָה עַל דֶּרֶךְ הָאֱמֶת,
and even though astronomically it is not the true physical moment of the equinox,
הֲרֵי הָיְתָה קַבָּלָתָם שֶׁנִּסְמוֹךְ עַל זֶה לְכָל דָּבָר כְּאִלּוּ הִיא הָיְתָה הַתְּקוּפָה בֶּאֱמֶת,
behold their tradition dictates that we rely upon this for all purposes as if it were the true equinox,
כֵּן נִרְאֶה בָּרוּר לְעַנִיּוּת דַּעְתִּי:
so it appears clear in my humble opinion:

sections.en: The Spiritual Meaning of the Two Equinoxes

p: וּבְדֶרֶךְ הַדְּרוּשׁ וְהָרֶמֶז אָמַרְתִּי בְּעִנְיַן שְׁתֵּי הַתְּקוּפוֹת מַה עִנְיָנָם,
And by way of homiletic exposition and mystical allusion I explained the significance of the two equinoxes,
וְגַם מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ: "תְּקוּפַת שְׁמוּאֵל בְּפַרְהֶסְיָא וּתְקוּפַת רַב אַדָּא בְּצִנְעָא".
and likewise their dictum: 'Shmuel's equinox in public, and Rav Adda's equinox in private.'
וְהַמְּפָרֵשׁ לְהִלְכוֹת קִדּוּשׁ הַחֹדֶשׁ (רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק י) כָּתַב
And the commentator on Hilchot Kiddush HaChodesh (beginning of chapter 10) wrote
שֶׁלֹּא גִּילוּ עֵת עוֹנָתָהּ בֶּאֱמֶת מִפְּנֵי הַמְכַשְּׁפִים;

Explanation — Water at a tekufah Some older customs express concern about water that was left uncovered at a seasonal turning point. This is a report of historical custom and belief, not a modern scientific statement that water becomes harmful at an equinox or solstice.

we hold that the first Nisan equinox preceded its conjunction by 7 days, 9 hours, 642 parts,

Explanation — How to read a tekufah–molad interval The figures measure the distance between a calculated solar-season boundary and a mean lunar conjunction. “7 days, 9 hours, 642 parts” means seven complete days plus nine hours and 642/1080 of an hour. Another model may give only “9 hours, 642 parts.” The debate concerns the model’s chosen starting point, not two different meanings of a chelek.

Explanation — Four seasonal time positions Because Shmuel’s annual cycle adds exactly one quarter of a day beyond 365 days, successive annual equinoxes recur at four possible six-hour divisions of the day. References to four quadrants or quarters of the day reflect that simplified timing pattern. Rav Adda’s finer fractional reckoning does not stay confined to those same four clock positions.
